title: Mathlib Imports for Graph Theory
content: Imports Mathlib's simple graph framework including clique detection, real number analysis, and logarithmic functions. The formalization uses SimpleGraph for the graph-theoretic structure and Real.log for the asymptotic bounds involving k² log k.
mathContext: We need $\text{SimpleGraph}$ for adjacency, $\text{Clique}$ for triangle detection, $\mathbb{R}$ for asymptotic bounds, and $\log$ for the $k^2 \log k$ growth rate.

title: Triangle-Free Graph
content: A graph is triangle-free if it contains no clique of size 3, i.e., no three mutually adjacent vertices. This is the local constraint that makes achieving high chromatic number require many vertices. Triangle-freeness eliminates the simplest obstruction to 2-colorability, making chromatic number growth depend on subtler structural properties.
mathContext: $G$ is triangle-free iff $\nexists\, a,b,c \in V(G)$ pairwise distinct with $ab, bc, ac \in E(G)$. Equivalently, $\omega(G) \leq 2$ where $\omega$ is the clique number.

title: Proper k-Coloring
content: A proper k-coloring assigns colors from {0,...,k-1} to vertices such that adjacent vertices receive different colors. This definition uses Fin k as the color set, making the coloring constraint a function with a pairwise inequality condition on adjacent vertices.
mathContext: A proper $k$-coloring is $f: V(G) \to [k]$ with $f(u) \neq f(v)$ whenever $uv \in E(G)$. The graph $G$ is $k$-colorable iff such $f$ exists.

title: Chromatic Number
content: The chromatic number χ(G) is the minimum k for which G has a proper k-coloring. Defined here as the supremum of k values for which G is not k-colorable, plus one. Computing χ(G) is NP-hard in general, but structural results (like triangle-freeness) constrain how χ relates to the vertex count.
mathContext: $\chi(G) = \min\{k : G \text{ is } k\text{-colorable}\} = \sup\{k : G \text{ is not } k\text{-colorable}\} + 1$

title: h₃(k) — Triangle-Free Chromatic Threshold
content: h₃(k) is the smallest n such that there exists a triangle-free graph on n vertices with chromatic number ≥ k. Equivalently, it is the minimum vertex count needed to realize chromatic number k under the triangle-free constraint. This is the central quantity of the problem—finding its asymptotic growth rate.
mathContext: $h_3(k) = \min\{n : \exists\, G \text{ on } n \text{ vertices},\, \omega(G) \leq 2,\, \chi(G) \geq k\}$. Mycielski's theorem guarantees $h_3(k) < \infty$ for all $k$.

title: Asymptotic Formula Conjecture
content: Erdős conjectured that h₃(k) is asymptotic to c·k²·log k for some constant c > 0. The known bounds place c ∈ [1/2, 1]. Determining the exact value of c would resolve one of the fundamental questions about how local structure (triangle-freeness) constrains global chromatic behavior.
mathContext:
$$\frac{h_3(k)}{k^2 \log k} \to c \quad \text{as } k \to \infty, \quad c \in [1/2, 1]$$
The lower bound uses probabilistic deletion; the upper bound uses explicit algebraic constructions.

title: Ratio Convergence Conjecture
content: The ratio h₃(k+1)/h₃(k) → 1 as k → ∞, meaning the threshold grows smoothly. This would follow from the asymptotic formula h₃(k) ~ c·k²·log k, since consecutive values of k²·log k have ratio approaching 1. However, it could also hold even without knowing the exact constant c.
mathContext:
$$\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{h_3(k+1)}{h_3(k)} = 1$$
If $h_3(k) \sim c k^2 \log k$, then $h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) \sim (k+1)^2 \log(k+1) / (k^2 \log k) \to 1$.

title: Lower Bound: (1/2 − o(1))k² log k
content: Any triangle-free graph on fewer than approximately k²·(log k)/2 vertices has chromatic number less than k. This is proved using the probabilistic method: a random k-coloring of a triangle-free graph has expected properties that force the chromatic number to be small relative to the vertex count. The key insight is that triangle-freeness limits the density of neighborhoods.
mathContext:
$$h_3(k) \geq \left(\frac{1}{2} - o(1)\right) k^2 \log k$$
For any $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $k$: $h_3(k) \geq (1/2 - \varepsilon) k^2 \log k$.

title: Upper Bound: (1 + o(1))k² log k
content: There exist explicit triangle-free graph constructions on approximately k²·log k vertices with chromatic number k. These constructions typically use algebraic or geometric methods—placing vertices on algebraic varieties and defining adjacency via arithmetic conditions that prevent triangles while maintaining high chromatic number.
mathContext:
$$h_3(k) \leq (1 + o(1)) k^2 \log k$$
For any $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $k$: $h_3(k) \leq (1 + \varepsilon) k^2 \log k$.

title: Graver–Yackel (1968) Early Lower Bound
content: Graver and Yackel (1968) gave the first quantitative lower bound on h₃(k) using probabilistic deletion: h₃(k) ≫ k²·(log k/log log k). This was later improved to the (1/2 − o(1))·k²·log k bound, removing the log log k factor in the denominator. Their work pioneered the probabilistic approach to triangle-free chromatic thresholds.
mathContext:
$$h_3(k) \geq c \cdot k^2 \cdot \frac{\log k}{\log \log k}$$
Weaker than the current best $(1/2 - o(1))k^2 \log k$ by a factor of $\log \log k$.

title: Monotonicity of h₃
content: h₃ is non-decreasing: if j ≤ k, then h₃(j) ≤ h₃(k). This is immediate since any triangle-free graph with χ ≥ k also has χ ≥ j, so the minimum vertex count for chromatic number ≥ k is at least that for ≥ j. Monotonicity is a basic structural property needed for the ratio convergence conjecture.
mathContext: $j \leq k \implies h_3(j) \leq h_3(k)$, since $\chi(G) \geq k \implies \chi(G) \geq j$.

title: Small Cases: h₃(1) through h₃(4)
content: The base cases anchor the asymptotic theory: h₃(1)=1 (single vertex, χ=1), h₃(2)=2 (edge K₂, χ=2), h₃(3)=5 (the 5-cycle C₅, the smallest triangle-free graph with χ=3), and h₃(4)=11 (the Grötzsch graph, also called the Mycielski graph M₄). These values appear in OEIS A292528 and match the Mycielski construction outputs.
mathContext: $h_3(1)=1$, $h_3(2)=2$, $h_3(3)=5$ ($C_5$), $h_3(4)=11$ (Grötzsch graph). The Mycielski graph $M_k$ has $3 \cdot 2^{k-2} - 1$ vertices.

title: Mycielski's Construction (1955)
content: Jan Mycielski's 1955 construction proves that triangle-free graphs of arbitrarily high chromatic number exist, making h₃(k) finite for all k. The Mycielskian operation takes a triangle-free graph G with χ(G) = k and produces a triangle-free graph G' with χ(G') = k+1, by adding a copy of the vertex set plus one extra vertex. Starting from K₂ gives the sequence M₂=K₂, M₃=C₅, M₄=Grötzsch graph, etc.
mathContext: For all $k \geq 2$: $\exists\, n, G$ on $n$ vertices with $\omega(G) \leq 2$ and $\chi(G) \geq k$. The Mycielskian $\mu(G)$ satisfies $\chi(\mu(G)) = \chi(G) + 1$ and preserves triangle-freeness. $|V(M_k)| = 3 \cdot 2^{k-2} - 1$.
